원.forms: Sino-Korean number + 원: 천 원 · 만 원
원.e: Originally 'round', for round coins — same root as Japanese yen and Chinese yuan.
원.t: Ask prices with 얼마예요? 10,000원 is 만 원, not 일만 원.

말.x: What that person said is right.
말.e: 말하다 = to speak. Say it longer for 'words'.
말.t: Homonym: 말 also means 'horse'. For elders' words use 말씀: 선생님 말씀.

말.forms: 말이 · 말을 (usually after a time word: 이번 달 말)
말.ex: 이번 달 말에 친구들과 여행을 가요.
말.x: I'm going on a trip with friends at the end of this month.
말.e: Homonym warning: other 말 words mean 'speech' and 'horse'.
말.t: It follows a time word: 이번 달 말, 학기 말; compounds include 주말, 월말, 연말.

말.x: Last summer I rode a horse for the first time on Jeju Island.
말.e: Homonym: 말 also means 'words, speech'; context tells you which.
말.t: Older speakers say speech 말 with a long vowel and horse 말 short; most young speakers no longer distinguish them.

회사원.x: My older brother is an office worker.

교과서.x: Please open your textbook to page 20.

쓰레기.x: Please throw the trash away over there.
쓰레기.e: Probably from 쓸다 (to sweep). 쓰레기통 = trash can.

부르다.forms: 불러요 · 불렀어요 · 부를 거예요 · 부르세요 (르 irregular)
부르다.m: to call (out); to sing; to be full (stomach, as 배가 부르다)
부르다.x: I sang songs at the karaoke room.
부르다.t: 노래를 부르다 = to sing a song; 배가 불러요 = I'm full.

비싸다.e: 비싸요! = 'It's expensive!' — handy at markets. Opposite: 싸다.

에.forms: place + 에 가다/오다/있다 (학교에 가요) · time + 에 (세 시에)
에.x: I go to the library on Saturday.
에.e: 학교에 가요 = I go to school; 세 시에 = at three o'clock.
에.t: Use 에 with destinations and with 있다/없다; use 에서 for where an action happens. No 에 after 오늘, 내일, 어제.

태우다.m: to give (someone) a ride, to pick up
태우다.ex: 아빠가 저를 차에 태워서 학교에 데려다주셨어요.
태우다.x: My dad gave me a ride to school in his car.
태우다.e: Causative of 타다 (to ride): 'make someone ride.' A separate 태우다 means 'to burn.'

사계절.ex: 한국에는 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울 사계절이 있어요.
사계절.x: Korea has four seasons: spring, summer, fall, and winter.
사계절.t: Koreans often say 사계절이 뚜렷해요, 'the four seasons are distinct,' when describing Korea.

짐.x: My luggage was so heavy that it was tough at the airport.
짐.e: Also figurative: 짐이 되다 'to be a burden' on someone.

만지다.x: Please don't touch the artwork with your hands in the museum.

외국인 등록증.ex: 한국에 90일 넘게 살면 외국인 등록증이 필요해요.
외국인 등록증.x: If you live in Korea for more than 90 days, you need a residence card.

평등.x: Gender equality is an important issue.
평등.e: Literally 'even rank' — everyone on the same level.

통화 중.forms: 통화 중이에요 · 통화 중이라서 (because the line is busy)
통화 중.m: on the phone, (the line is) busy
통화 중.x: I called, but the line was busy the whole time.
통화 중.e: Literally 'in the middle of a call'; -중 = in the middle of: 회의 중, 수업 중.

보너스.ex: 올해 연말에 회사에서 보너스를 많이 받았어요.
보너스.x: I got a big bonus from my company at the end of this year.

즐거워하다.x: The kids had a great time at the amusement park all day.
즐거워하다.e: From 즐겁다 'joyful' plus -어하다, showing someone else's enjoyment.

사고방식.x: People's ways of thinking differ a little from country to country.

폭넓다.x: She has broad experience, so she gives good advice.
폭넓다.e: 폭 'width' + native 넓다 'wide' — literally 'wide in width'.
폭넓다.t: Pronounced [퐁널따]: ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ, and ㄼ sounds as ㄹ.

별자리.ex: 맑은 날 밤에는 시골에서 별자리를 볼 수 있어요.
별자리.x: On clear nights you can see the constellations in the countryside.
별자리.e: Native: 별 'star' + 자리 'place, seat' — a star's place in the sky.
별자리.t: Pronounced [별짜리]: the ㅈ of 자리 is said tense in this compound (a sai-sori effect, not a rule triggered by ㄹ). It also means a Western star sign: 무슨 별자리예요? 'What's your star sign?'

헐.forms: casual exclamation · 헐, 대박! · 헐, 진짜?
헐.m: what?!, OMG, no way (shock or disbelief)
헐.x: What?! The tickets are already sold out?
헐.e: A stunned sound word that spread through internet chat in the 2000s and moved into everyday speech.
헐.t: Casual: fine with friends, not with bosses or elders. It can greet good or bad news but usually carries dismay or disbelief.

뿐.forms: N뿐이에요 · N뿐(만) 아니라 (not only N) · after verbs: -(으)ㄹ 뿐이에요
뿐.ex: 우리 반에서 안경 쓴 사람은 저뿐이에요.
뿐.x: I'm the only one in our class who wears glasses.
뿐.e: Native word. After a noun it's a particle (저뿐); after a verb it's a bound noun written with a space (웃을 뿐이에요).
뿐.t: 뿐 is almost always followed by 이다 or 아니라: 저뿐이에요 'it's only me'; 한국어뿐만 아니라 영어도 'not only Korean but also English'.

세무서.ex: 세금 문제 때문에 세무서에 가야 해요.
세무서.x: I have to go to the tax office about a tax issue.

합병.ex: 두 은행이 합병해서 하나의 큰 은행이 되었습니다.
합병.x: The two banks merged and became one large bank.
합병.t: Pronounced [합뼝]: ㅂ makes the next consonant tense.

급성.x: Last night I went to the ER with acute gastroenteritis.

해수면.ex: 빙하가 녹아서 해수면이 계속 높아지고 있어요.
해수면.x: Sea levels keep rising as glaciers melt.
해수면.t: In the news you'll hear 해수면 상승 = sea-level rise.

고마움.ex: 졸업식 날 선생님께 고마움을 전하고 싶어요.
고마움.x: I want to express my gratitude to my teacher on graduation day.
고마움.e: Noun from 고맙다 'thankful': ㅂ becomes 우, then -ㅁ is added.
고마움.t: Common patterns: 고마움을 전하다 or 고마움을 표현하다 'to express gratitude'.

발코니.x: The weather was nice, so I dried the laundry on the balcony.
발코니.e: From English 'balcony'. In Korean apartments it is usually enclosed with windows.

커버 댄스.ex: 주말마다 친구들이랑 커버 댄스 영상을 찍어요.
커버 댄스.x: Every weekend I film cover dance videos with my friends.
커버 댄스.e: From English 'cover' + 'dance': copying an existing song's choreography, like a cover song.
커버 댄스.t: Popular with K-pop fans worldwide; dance studios run classes for it, and people film 커버 댄스 in public places.

쩝쩝.ex: 밥 먹을 때 쩝쩝 소리 내지 마세요.
쩝쩝.x: Please don't smack your lips when you eat.
쩝쩝.e: 의성어 (sound word) for loud chewing with an open mouth.
쩝쩝.t: Loud chewing is considered rude in Korea, so 쩝쩝거리다 is usually a complaint. Single 쩝 also shows mild disappointment.

완제품.ex: 이 공장은 부품을 수입해서 완제품을 만듭니다.
완제품.x: This factory imports parts and makes finished products.

무덤덤하다.x: Even when she was praised, her face showed no emotion.
무덤덤하다.e: Built on 덤덤하다 'calm, unmoved', but showing even less reaction.

개발자.ex: 제 친구는 게임 회사에서 개발자로 일해요.
개발자.x: My friend works as a developer at a game company.
개발자.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.
개발자.t: Pronounced [개발짜] — the ㅈ is tensed after ㄹ.

집행유예.x: He was sentenced to one year in prison, suspended for two years.
집행유예.e: Literally 'hesitating on execution' — the sentence is held off unless you reoffend.
집행유예.t: Headlines often shorten it to 집유, e.g. 징역 2년 집유 3년.

병합.x: In 1910, Japan forcibly annexed the Korean Empire.

탈구조주의.ex: 탈구조주의는 텍스트의 의미가 고정되어 있지 않다고 봅니다.
탈구조주의.x: Post-structuralism holds that the meaning of a text is not fixed.
탈구조주의.t: 탈- is a productive prefix for 'post-' or 'de-': 탈원전 (nuclear phase-out), 탈권위 (anti-authoritarian).

역학조사.ex: 보건 당국은 확진자의 동선에 대한 역학조사를 실시했습니다.
역학조사.x: Health authorities carried out an epidemiological investigation into the patient's movements.

유전체.ex: 축전기의 두 금속판 사이에는 유전체가 들어 있습니다.
유전체.x: In a capacitor, there is a dielectric between the two metal plates.
유전체.t: Homonym alert: in biology 유전체 (with different hanja) means 'genome'.

공공연히.ex: 그 회사의 문제는 업계에서 공공연히 알려져 있어요.
공공연히.x: That company's problems are openly known in the industry.
공공연히.e: Literally 'public, public-ly': done right out in the open.

유상증자.ex: 그 회사는 유상증자로 천억 원을 마련했습니다.
유상증자.x: The company raised 100 billion won through a rights offering.
유상증자.e: Literally 'paid capital increase': shareholders pay money for the new shares.

낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.de: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.rom: nammareun saega deutgo bammareun jwiga deunneunda
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.pr: 난마른 새가 듣꼬 밤마른 쥐가 든는다
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.forms: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다고 · 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다잖아요
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.m: walls have ears; be careful what you say (lit. birds hear daytime words and mice hear nighttime words)
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.ex: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다고, 회사에서 상사 험담은 하지 마세요.
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.x: Walls have ears, so don't badmouth your boss at work.
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.e: Literally 'birds hear what is said by day, and mice hear what is said by night': someone is always listening.
낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.t: Pronounced [난마른 새가 듣꼬 밤마른 쥐가 든는다]. A warning to watch what you say, especially gossip and secrets.

nb: 열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다
